Alice / Vanessa — attaching the sizing matrix and a short runbook. High-level summary below and full details in the attachments.

Summary:
- Private (VPC private control plane): recommended pilot footprint = 2x A100-80GB equiv nodes (reserved for load balancing/maintenance) with autoscale policy to add up to 4 nodes during peak. Initial reserved compute lead time: ~8–10 weeks if procurement includes on-prem hardware; if deploying into customer VPC on cloud, lead time is ~2–3 weeks for private onboarding.
- Dedicated (Redwood reserved capacity): recommended pilot = 1 reserved shard sized at 4 concurrent workers (effectively 1.5 A100-80GB equiv or cheaper quantized variant) with burst capacity available. Lead time: ~3–5 business days.

Economic delta (pilot): Dedicated shows ~35–45% lower TCO per token for average steady-state due to pooling and Redwood instance-level optimizations; Private has higher fixed cost but gives stronger network and control-plane isolation. For your burst profile, Dedicated can meet latency SLO with our burst lanes but requires contractual SLAs for guaranteed burst capacity.

Breakglass runbook gist:
- Normal: VPC private control plane routes requests to private shard.
- If private control-plane becomes unavailable or suspected compromise: failover to a Dedicated, reduced-capability model variant with explicit redaction pre-step (strip attachments / mask PHI) and logging-forward to your SIEM.
- Fallback path leverages pre-provisioned minimal Dedicated pool (warm standby) and a tokenized ingress tunnel; full runbook attached.

Attachments: lockbox_sizing_matrix.xlsx (matrix + numbers), breakglass_runbook.md, soc2_evidence_summary.pdf

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
